Rockwell Automation.why: Supplies data-center power and cooling infrastructure - CUBIC modular power distribution, motor control centers and medium-voltage drives sold with chiller OEMs, and Logix controllers for central utility plants (energy monitoring, emergency power, backup generator controls); data center was one of its strongest double-digit growth verticals in Q3 FY2026, so its sales grow with AI data-center construction.
Rockwell Automation.evidence: CEO Blake Moret (Q3 FY2026 call): 'three main areas of data center participation for Rockwell: there's the power distribution through our modular CUBIC design ... our participation with the chiller manufacturers in terms of power control, so think motor control centers, big drives, medium-voltage drives with the chiller OEMs. And then there's the work that Logix is increasingly being used for, primarily in the central utility plant.'

players.product: CUBIC modular power-distribution systems, motor control centers, medium-voltage drives and Logix controllers for data-center power, cooling and central utility plants

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026: reported sales up 8% and organic sales up 10% year-over-year, above the company's expectations; the Sensia dissolution (effective April 1, completed smoothly and on schedule) decreased sales by 3% and currency contributed about 1% of growth; price contributed approximately 1%. Enterprise operating margin 22.3%, up 280 basis points (about 40 basis points from the Sensia dissolution), on higher volume and favorable mix partly offset by negative price/cost; gross margin 49.5% (+70 basis points). Adjusted EPS $3.49, up more than 20%; free cash flow $654 million, $165 million higher than the prior year. CEO Blake Moret: products continue to outperform the longer-cycle solutions business, with smaller modernization projects across most industries driving the majority of growth; the verticals with the strongest capital investment (semiconductor, data center, e-commerce & warehouse) are weighted toward product and software offerings. North America was the strongest region at 12% growth and is expected to be the fastest-growing region for fiscal 2026. Total incremental margin was in the high 50s as reported and over 40% organic, the fourth consecutive quarter above 40%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 FY2026 reported sales +8%, organic +10%; enterprise operating margin 22.3%; adjusted EPS $3.49; free cash flow $654 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 by segment: Intelligent Devices organic sales up 10% with broad-based growth across all product lines; new offerings such as PointMax I/O, additional PowerFlex drives and FLEXLINE motor control centers are seeing strong adoption, particularly in e-commerce & warehouse automation and process industries; the Production Logistics business grew double digits with strategic wins across food & beverage, semiconductor and life sciences; segment margin 20%, up 120 basis points but lower than expected as inflation partly offset higher sales, currency and mix. Software & Control organic sales up 18%, driven by another quarter of strong double-digit growth in Logix; segment margin 34.8%, up 320 basis points and above expectations (incrementals about 50%). Lifecycle Services organic sales down 2%, generally in line with expectations, constrained by the lack of capital spending recovery in food & beverage and certain process industries; segment margin 15.1%, up 180 basis points, helped by the Sensia dissolution. Organic annual recurring revenue grew 6%, below expectations: high-single-digit software growth (Plex included) was partially offset by slower recurring Lifecycle Services.
quarterly_data.figure: Intelligent Devices organic +10%, margin 20%; Software & Control organic +18%, margin 34.8%; Lifecycle Services organic down 2%, margin 15.1%; organic ARR +6%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Blake Moret on data center: it remained a strong growth market in Q3, with customers investing in the power, cooling, automation and control systems required to support increasingly complex and energy-intensive facilities. He described three main areas of participation: (1) power distribution through the modular CUBIC design, from the acquisition of a Danish company a few years ago; (2) power control with chiller manufacturers - motor control centers, big drives and medium-voltage drives with the chiller OEMs; (3) Logix controllers, used primarily in the central utility plant for energy monitoring, emergency power and backup generator controls, where Logix's inherent redundancy and safety characteristics are not available in traditional distributed digital controller (DDC) units. He sees increasing standardization on these units by hyperscalers and contractors building modular, very repeatable designs to increase speed to capacity, and additional share growth in data center applications on top of strong overall data center growth. Excluding everything related to data center, Q3 organic growth would still have been 8% (versus 10% in total). On fiscal 2027: 'Data center makes its own weather' and 'We expect data center to keep on keeping on.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 organic growth 8% excluding data center (10% in total)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 by industry: discrete sales grew high teens, led by strong double-digit growth in semiconductor, data center and e-commerce & warehouse; automotive up low double digits, better than expected; e-commerce & warehouse automation up 30% with strong performance across regions and customer segments; semiconductor driven by increased activity from several leading equipment manufacturers and chip makers, including continued investment tied to AI infrastructure. Hybrid industries grew mid-single digits: food & beverage up mid-single digits, led by North America, without an inflection in large capital projects; life sciences up 10% with broad-based growth across regions. Process up high single digits, led by energy, metals and chemicals: energy up high single digits on brownfield expansions, asset modernization and production optimization, with healthy activity across LNG, midstream, power infrastructure and offshore supported by the build-out of power capacity for data centers and electrification; mining down mid-single digits on measured capital deployment and project timing delays in Latin America. CEO: customers are turning to Rockwell's portfolio for GLP-1 related investments, evolving food and beverage demand, AI-driven data center growth and new opportunities across energy storage, defense and advanced manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: discrete up high teens; e-commerce & warehouse automation +30%; life sciences +10%; process up high single digits; mining down mid-single digits

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2026 guidance raised: reported and organic sales growth 7.5% to 9.5% (8.5% midpoint, up 150 basis points from the prior guide), assuming modest sequential growth in Q4; at the midpoint, reported growth includes about 150 basis points of favorable currency offset by the Sensia dissolution. CEO: the top-line guide is at the higher end of the midterm growth framework. Adjusted EPS $13 to $13.30 (midpoint $13.15, up $0.35, about 25% growth versus fiscal 2025). Enterprise operating margin still expected at 21.5%, up 260 basis points; organic ARR growth mid-single digits; free cash flow conversion 100%; about 250 basis points of price realization (about 100 from tariff-related pricing, about 150 underlying), with tariffs EPS-neutral; full-year incrementals above 50% as reported and high 40s organic. Q4: total reported sales up low single digits sequentially with enterprise operating margin about flat versus Q3, on higher inflation and unfavorable mix as configure-to-order and solutions sales reach their seasonal peak. Full-year segments: Intelligent Devices reported revenue up low double digits, margin around 20%; Software & Control up high teens, margin in the low 30s (Q4 around 33, lower sequentially on flat sales as memory inflation hits this segment hardest); Lifecycle Services revenue down about $150 million (Sensia dissolution and longer-cycle headwinds), margin flat to slightly up. Capex about 3% of sales; engineering and development about 8% of sales. Results and guidance exclude any expected IEEPA refunds or claims resulting from the Supreme Court decision.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 reported and organic sales growth 7.5% to 9.5% (midpoint 8.5%); adjusted EPS $13 to $13.30 (midpoint $13.15); enterprise operating margin 21.5%; free cash flow conversion 100%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Christian Rothe on inflation and supply: inflation began with memory earlier this fiscal year and continues to broaden; data center demand is affecting several areas, memory being the biggest. The top priority is securing components and maintaining availability, and the supply chain team has kept production unimpacted. The inflation headwind was single-digit millions in Q1 and double-digit millions in Q2, and is still a double-digit millions headwind for the second half, higher than reported last quarter; he does not expect it to stabilize soon. Core price/cost was unfavorable in Q3 (rising costs and the timing of price increases); an inflation-based price increase implemented late in Q3 will be realized in Q4, and price/cost is expected to be positive for Q4 and the full year. Memory cost and inflation will hit Software & Control hardest going into fiscal 2027: at mid-30s segment margins 'it's really hard to get margin expansion from price alone', though volume should help. CEO: structural changes from the earlier shortage period help - a fixed discount methodology with distribution partners for faster price realization, more frequent price changes, and alternate sources for some materials to introduce competition.
quarterly_data.figure: production not impacted; inflation headwind double-digit millions in the second half, increasing

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2027 (initial outlook to be given next quarter). CEO tailwinds: the broadening of growing verticals, which he sees no reason to slow; data center; renewed investment in automotive and life sciences; home & personal care was good in the quarter; labor costs and shortages driving automation as America seeks to bring more manufacturing on board; new product introductions to keep taking share; continued aggressive productivity and pricing actions. Headwinds: inflation 'is not going to go away', continued tariff volatility and geopolitical uncertainty. CEO: Logix controller unit shipments are only now getting back to pre-COVID levels and will exceed that unit volume this year; he believes Rockwell is gaining share in controllers. CFO: fiscal 2027 capex will be higher than fiscal 2026 but 'still going to stay in that 4% or so'; investment in the greenfield project in New Berlin, Wisconsin will start at pace in fiscal 2027 and continue into fiscal 2028; ROIC has recovered nicely and EBITDA continues to grow.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 capex above FY2026 (about 3% of sales); CFO: 'still going to stay in that 4% or so'

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and wins: CFO: Q3 book-to-bill was inside the company's normal corridor (it had been slightly above it the prior quarter), order development is consistent with sales and 'the book-to-bill is in good shape'; Lifecycle Services book-to-bill was 0.97. Notable Q3 wins: a large automotive brand owner selected Rockwell's end-to-end automation portfolio to improve operational efficiency and accelerate the launch of future vehicle programs across multiple global plants; a leading pharmaceutical and biotech contract development and manufacturing organization chose Rockwell's integrated process control and MES platform to standardize drug substance manufacturing across its operations. CEO: important competitive wins with standardization on Rockwell's architecture around the world, including large automotive brand owners outside Rockwell's traditional end customers, and increasing competitive MES wins in drug substance.
quarterly_data.figure: Lifecycle Services book-to-bill 0.97; total book-to-bill inside the normal corridor

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on capital spending: no broad-based recovery in large capital projects yet; capex has not picked up in food & beverage (the single biggest vertical) and parts of process, while automotive and life sciences show early signs of renewed project activity. Reasons customers give for project delays: a cautious approach to deploying capital, delaying important but not urgent projects, high levels of decision authority for approvals, funding constraints (capital projects in Latin America) and terms and conditions amid tariff and inflation volatility; tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty continue to delay large greenfield projects while modernization spending remains strong. Automotive: green shoots of new projects as automakers refocus from the electric-vehicle surge to hybrids and internal-combustion vehicles, with model changes driving the most spend ('not ready to say the flood gates are open'). Life sciences: a multiyear trend, with GLP-1 drugs, including oral solid dose variants, driving additional automation need.

CEO on production logistics and software: Rockwell is early in the production logistics growth opportunity (moving material to and from the make line in consumer packaged goods, plus semiconductor wafer transport and life sciences); iTRAK and MagneMotion independent cart technology are having a good year; autonomous mobile robots will see another year of strong double-digit growth, and Rockwell expects Clearpath to be profitable in the fourth quarter. Plex (part of software ARR, up high single digits) continues to add new logos across automotive tier suppliers and consumer, has expanded into consumer-packaged goods as planned, is very profitable, and embeds agentic AI throughout its modules; Rockwell is integrating Plex and traditional MES with fleet management from its mobility business and mobile robots for orchestration.

Customer Unilever expanded its cybersecurity program with Rockwell to additional sites, cited by the CEO as an important ARR win; the engagement combines Rockwell's threat detection and secure remote access software with managed cybersecurity services to provide continuous monitoring, secure connectivity and protection of critical manufacturing operations.

Customer Convergix, a global system integrator, chose Rockwell's Emulate3D digital twin software to model a complex conveyance system, helping reduce project risk, accelerate commissioning and bring production online faster (cited by the CEO as an example of strong modernization spending).
